segments.name: Gene editing technology
segments.description: Develops and commercializes CRISPR-based gene editing medicines, including in vivo therapies, for patients with serious diseases.
segments.evidence: The CEO views the Company's operations and manages the Company's business as one operating segment, which is the business of developing and commercializing gene editing technology.

revenueModel.text: The company earns collaboration and other research and development revenues from license and collaboration partners, including upfront and annual license fees under agreements such as the Vertex License Agreement.
revenueModel.evidence: the Vertex License Agreement further provides for the payment by Vertex of a potential additional $50.0 million contingent upfront payment and further future fixed and sales-based annual license fees, ranging from $5.0 million to $40.0 million annually, inclusive of certain sales-based annual license fee increases, through 2034.

changes.text: In December 2024, the company decided not to pursue commercialization of reni-cel, its ex vivo gene-edited medicine for sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia.
changes.evidence: we determined in December 2024 not to pursue commercialization for reni-cel in order to optimize our cost structure and accelerate our intent to achieve human proof of concept of our in vivo gene editing medicines.
